brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A pan-fired green tea from gardens at 1420 metres beside Mahu Lake in Leibo county, Liangshan, Sichuan.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is recorded as a tribute tea in the Qing dynasty. Little more is documented about its history.
processing: Spread for 1 to 2 hours, then fixed, and rolled and pan-fired in turn at falling heat. Rubbed by hand into balls to bring out the down, then broken up and dried slowly over charcoal at 70 to 80°C.
harvest_season: Before Qingming; one bud with one or two young leaves.
appearance_dry: Tight, fine and straight, with visible tips and an oily sheen.
taste_profile: Fresh, strong, mellow and brisk, with fragrance.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
